sub_scenario.one_line: podcast audio engineer: the record likely holds in the reserved suite

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the mix session and closing stale entries.
The episode masters review wrapped early today.
Field recording days, unpredictable by nature, are handled fine with monitoring headphones.
Someone new shadowed me in the treated studio this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the broadcast specs into one message before lunch.
My mixes pass broadcast spec on first submission because they are made in my treated studio; the network's QC log shows two years without a single bounce.
The treated room is the QC record.
The record and the room are the same fact.
Editorial calls and content reviews happen anywhere without cost.
I archived last cycle's notes on the episode masters and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
First-submission pass rates directly determine which engineers get the flagship shows.
A vendor call about the mix session ran long but ended well.
I walked through the treated studio checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the broadcast specs.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the episode masters records and fixed it at the source.
The network's new production hub includes a certified mix suite with my show days reserved in the booking system; the suite's measurements match my studio within tolerance.
The hub reproduces your mechanism, reserved.
Reserved in writing, measured within tolerance.
I sketched next week's plan for the broadcast specs before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the mix session updates.
The hub also puts me two floors from the editorial team I mix for.
A freelance friend says production hubs always end in hot-desking chaos within a year.
Prophecy without a booking system in evidence.
I closed the week by updating the treated studio handover notes.
The move to the production hub is confirmed for next quarter. How is my first-submission record likely to fare?
